newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Foreign stock investment in Seoul soars in May.
newsitem.headline: Foreign stock investment in Seoul soars in May.

text.p: South Korea said on Thursday foreign stock buying in May soared to 1.73 trillion won from 612.4 billion in April thanks to expansion of the foreign stockholding limit.
The Securities Supervisory Board (SSB) said foreign investors sold stocks worth 644.7 billion won in May, down from 746.5 billion in April.

As a result, net buying by foreigners was 1.09 trillion won in May, compared with net sales of 134.1 billion in April, the SSB said. On May 2, South Korea raised the foreign stock ownership limit to 23 percent of a stock from 20 percent.
The SSB said foreign stock trading accounted for 7.08 percent of the market's total trading in May, against 4.47 percent in April.

Investors from the U.S. led the way by buying 490.6 billion won worth and selling 134.1 billion worth. Malaysian investors followed with 345.9 billion won in buying and 164.3 billion in sales, the SSB said.
By stock, Samsung Electronics topped the list of popular stocks among foreigners, whose net buying of the stock was 176.2 billion in May. Foreign net buying of POSCO was 140.2 billion won.
